newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle trade up $1 at $72 -trade.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle trade up $1 at $72 -trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded Wednesday at $72.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from a week ago, in active dealings, feedlot sources said.
About 35,000 head were estimated sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma areas, but could go higher as sales are tallied. Kansas feedlots also reportedly sold about 30,000 to 35,000 head.
Strong beef prices and tight supplies of finished cattle drove feedlot cattle prices up as expected, the sources said.
Tight supplies of finished cattle were attributed to lighter placements earlier in the year and active marketings.
Cattle owners were selling cattle as much as 30 days ahead of schedule as they take advantage of profitability due to lower feed costs and firm packer demand, market sources said.
Owners were earning about $100 per head at the $72.00 level, according to Dale Benson, analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds in Chicago.
Benson said he expected to see finished cattle supplies remain tight until December 10 when cattle placed into feedlots during August and September start coming on line.
